# UX and Accessibility

119 rules with do/don't and code examples in `references/guidelines.md`. Read
that file when you need detail — this page is the check order and the things
you should never have to look up.

**Scope:** how an interface *behaves*. For how it *looks* — scales, hierarchy,
colour, depth — use the `kx-design` skill instead. They do not overlap.

## Check order

Work down. A failure high on this list outranks anything below it.

| # | Area | Must hold |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accessibility | 4.5:1 contrast, alt text, keyboard reachable, visible focus, never colour alone |
| 2 | Touch & interaction | 24×24 CSS px minimum target (44×44 on mobile), no hover-only affordance |
| 3 | Forms & feedback | Visible label, error next to the field, loading state on submit |
| 4 | Layout & responsive | Mobile-first, no horizontal scroll, text reflows at 320px and 200% zoom |
| 5 | Animation | Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, animate transform/opacity only |
| 6 | Navigation | Predictable back, active state, no broken deep links |

## Non-negotiable

These fail an interface outright. Do not ship past them, and do not need the
reference to apply them.

- **Visible focus on every interactive control** — including inside modals.
  Removing an outline without replacing it is the single most common
  accessibility defect in React codebases.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` respected** wherever anything moves.
- **Labels are visible.** A placeholder is not a label; it disappears exactly
  when the user needs it.
- **Errors sit next to the field they describe**, not only in a summary at the
  top.
- **Never colour alone.** Add an icon, shape or text cue.
- **Text must reflow.** No fixed-height box clipping copy at 200% zoom.
- **A real `<button>`,** not a clickable `<div>`. Role, keyboard operation and
  state come free; reimplementing them never goes well.

## Applying it

Search the reference by category heading or rule name — the file is grouped by
category, most severe first:

```bash
grep -n "^### " references/guidelines.md          # every rule
grep -A6 "^## Forms" references/guidelines.md     # one category
```

A rule cites what to do, what not to do, and both code examples. Quote the
rule name when you report a violation so it can be checked.

## Severity, when reporting

The reference marks each rule Critical / High / Medium / Low. Map it straight
onto `kx-standards` severity: Critical and High block, Medium is a judgment call,
Low gets mentioned once.

An accessibility failure is a correctness bug, not a preference — it is the
one class of UI finding that carries the same weight as a logic error.
